title: Cross-service session stitching UI prototype for correlation-centered request investigation
creator: Riley Chen
description: Design and prototype a correlation-centered investigation workspace that stitches spans and logs across services into a single session timeline. The UI should make it trivial to investigate a customer-visible failure by entering a correlation id or selecting a request sample and then exploring spans, logs, and downstream downstream calls across services. Emphasize clarity when data is partial (sampling) and provide controls to toggle strict vs fuzzy correlation matching.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype screens in Figma demonstrating: correlation-id entry, fuzzy/strict toggle, combined timeline with service swimlanes, span detail side panel, and time-synced logs
Design includes an affordance for sampled/partial data and a lightweight explanation copy for users
Interaction spec for switching between single-request and aggregated sessions (grouped by correlation id)
Engineers have sign-off on required telemetry fields and a proposed pre-aggregation strategy to avoid expensive cross-service joins
Usability test run with >=5 platform engineers/product engineers and top 3 usability findings addressed
decisions: Use correlation id as primary key and allow fuzzy matching (prefix/subset) to surface related sessions; strict matching will be the default for exact investigations
Introduce server-side pre-aggregation for 24-hour sliding windows to power the combined session view to avoid per-request cross-service joins
Show sampled spans with a semitransparent overlay and a tooltip explaining sampling impact on completeness
Timeline will use sticky mini-map for long sessions and allow zoom-to-span; we will not implement replay at this stage to limit scope
engineering_feedback: ENG review (2026-03-03): Concerns about query cost for ad-hoc fuzzy correlation; recommend adding a max-lookup budget and defaulting to pre-aggregated indices
ENG note: Need explicit contract for correlation-id propagation headers in SDKs and a fallback heuristic for legacy services that use trace ids
Infra: must expose a sampling-confidence metric in the API so UI can accurately label partial sessions
usability_testing_notes: Session test with 5 backend engineers: all could find the root error quicker with the merged timeline vs jumping between service traces
Confusion observed when correlation id returned many matches; testers wanted an inline ranking by recency and error-rate
Participants expected a visible cost indicator when expanding large aggregated sessions; add a lightweight token/cost hint in the header
tradeoffs: Pre-aggregation improves UI responsiveness but may lag live events by up to 30s; tradeoff accepted for interactive exploration
Fuzzy matching helps discovery but can surface noisy unrelated sessions; mitigated with ranking and filters
Avoiding full replay reduces scope but defers deterministic debugging; planned as a follow-up workstream
next_steps: Incorporate ENG-provided telemetry contract into the Figma annotations (deadline 2026-03-16)
Update prototype to show recency/error-rate ranking for correlation matches (estimate 2 points)
Add cost token indicator in header and get PM approval on wording (Aisha)
Handoff session with runtime and infra teams to validate pre-aggregation feasibility (schedule 2026-03-18)
comments: 2026-02-26 - Riley Chen: Initial concept uploaded. Core idea: present a single investigation view for a correlation id that stitches spans across services into a single timeline. Open questions about data volume and sampling UX.
2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel (PM): Love the session-first approach — ask: can we surface estimated cost of expanding a match? Also prioritize quick path to jump from session to a specific span's logs.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Li (ENG): We reviewed the mock. Concern: fuzzy correlation queries could be very expensive. Proposal: build pre-aggregated correlation index with TTL and cap fuzzy matches to N=50 by default.
2026-03-06 - Riley Chen: Updated prototype to include fuzzy/strict toggle, sampling overlay, and a ranked match list. Uploaded to Figma and linked above.
2026-03-10 - Usability session: 5 engineers tested flows. Feedback: add inline match ranking and a quick filter to show only spans with errors/warnings. We'll iterate.
2026-03-12 - Design review scheduled. Requested: A11y check for timeline color palette and copy review for sampling disclosures. Next: incorporate ENG telemetry contract and address ranking UX.
